brief: Design an interface for a "Temporal Recipe Converter" that helps users adapt historical recipes from any era (1400s-present) to modern cooking methods, where the UI transforms like a time-dilating acc

dominant_strengths: Clean dark-mode hierarchy with restrained indigo accent gives the title and active era a clear focal anchor.
Ingredient cards have consistent rhythm, icon-to-text alignment is tidy, and the slider metaphor for eras is legible.
dominant_weaknesses: Fails the 'time-dilating' brief entirely — no temporal transformation, comparison view, or visual era-shifting; it's just a static list with a slider.
Emoji-style icons clash with the otherwise minimalist serious palette, undermining craft and any historical/temporal atmosphere.
Zero indication of what changes between eras — no before/after units, no measurement translation, no diegetic 'time' affordance beyond a label swap.
fix_priorities: Introduce a visible era transformation: split-view or morphing values (e.g., '2 handfuls → 500g') that animate as the slider moves.
Replace emoji icons with custom monoline glyphs that can stylistically shift per era (parchment/serif for Ancient, sans for Modern).
Add temporal texture — typographic era cues, subtle parchment/grain shifts, or method translation panel — to express the concept viscerally.
Tighten slider design: tick marks, era-specific accent color, and a year readout to reinforce dilation metaphor.
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral legibility is acceptable, but visceral atmosphere is flat and reflective payoff is missing because the temporal concept never manifests visually.
rationale.intent_fit: Only superficially solves the brief — the era slider exists but the recipe never actually 'converts' or transforms, so the core promise is unmet.
